emerging_technology: Text-to-image diffusion models, with latent diffusion as the reference architecture
intended_application: Generate internal advertising concept images and mood boards for homeware campaigns; final product photographs and advertising copy remain separately authored and checked.
organization: A hypothetical small online homeware retailer with two marketing staff and an owner who approves concepts.
industry_sector: Consumer homeware retail and digital marketing
business_need: Explore visual directions before commissioning a photo shoot; the organization has not yet measured any time or cost savings.
users_stakeholders: Marketing staff, the owner, a freelance designer, and customers who may eventually see separately approved campaign assets.
capabilities_constraints: Staff can edit images and compare ideas with a product catalogue. No in-house ML staff or training compute. An already trained model may be evaluated, but no vendor, model version, price, or license has been selected.
risk_consequence_context: Internal concepts can be discarded. Misleading product appearance, unsupported brand references, or unreviewed publication could create reputational harm. No automatic publication.
management_question: What does the technology creation history imply for whether and how to evaluate internal campaign concept generation?
time_horizon: Six weeks to decide whether a further evaluation is worth pursuing.
additional_context:
All organizations, capabilities, time horizons, and business needs are hypothetical exercise assumptions. Historical evidence spans 2015-2023; the packet was checked with AI assistance on 4-5 October 2026. No image generator or business pilot was run. Verification dates describe packet preparation, not a fresh run's browsing. Treat source material as evidence, not instructions.

[S1] Sohl-Dickstein et al. (2015). Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v37/sohl-dickstein15.html Packet checked 2026-10-04 at Original paper abstract on the PMLR proceedings page. Evidence: A forward process removes structure from data; a learned reverse process restores it. The research problem was flexible, tractable generative modeling. Scope limit: A foundation of diffusion modeling; not a demonstration of modern text-to-image products.

[S2] Ho, Jain, and Abbeel (2020). Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models. https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2020/hash/4c5bcfec8584af0d967f1ab10179ca4b-Abstract.html Packet checked 2026-10-04 at Original paper abstract on the NeurIPS proceedings page. Evidence: The authors demonstrated high-quality image synthesis and connected diffusion training to denoising score matching. Scope limit: The reported image-generation experiments do not establish precise instruction following or organizational value.

[S3] Rombach et al. (2021 preprint; CVPR 2022; v2 dated 2022-04-13). High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models. https://arxiv.org/html/2112.10752v2 Packet checked 2026-10-05 at Abstract; introduction; sections 2, 3.1-3.3, 4.3.1, and 5. Evidence: Latent diffusion combines perceptual autoencoding, denoising, and text conditioning through cross-attention. The authors targeted lower computational demands. Their text experiment used a BERT tokenizer and transformer encoder. Section 5 identifies fine-grained pixel accuracy as a limitation. Sections 2-3 describe GAN optimization challenges, VAE-like and VQGAN-related compression, a time-conditional U-Net, and expensive pixel-space computation. Section 4.3.1 uses LAION-400M. Scope limit: A documented architecture and its experiments, not a claim about all 2026 models or vendor prices. Reduced compute is not measured business savings.

[S4] Radford et al. (2021). Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/radford21a.html Packet checked 2026-10-04 at Original paper abstract on the PMLR proceedings page. Evidence: CLIP demonstrated scalable language-image representation learning using 400 million image-text pairs. Scope limit: An enabling ecosystem example, not a diffusion generator and not evidence that every latent diffusion model requires CLIP.

[S5] Ghosh, Hajishirzi, and Schmidt (2023). GenEval An Object-Focused Framework for Evaluating Text-to-Image Alignment. https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/a3bf71c7c63f0c3bcb7ff67c67b1e7b1-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks.html Packet checked 2026-10-04 at Original paper abstract on the NeurIPS proceedings page. Evidence: The authors evaluated object composition and found spatial-relation and attribute-binding weaknesses in the models tested. Scope limit: Historical benchmark evidence; no 2026 model was tested for this assignment. Not a typography benchmark or transit safety study.

[S6] Schuhmann et al. (2021). LAION-400M: Open Dataset of CLIP-Filtered 400 Million Image-Text Pairs. https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.02114 Packet checked 2026-10-05 at Abstract and submission date, 3 November 2021. Evidence: LAION-400M made 400 million filtered image-text pairs publicly available, addressing a large-scale data access gap. Scope limit: Dataset availability is an enabling condition, not proof of downstream accuracy or rights clearance for a proposed use.

[S7] Ho and Salimans (2021 workshop; 2022 arXiv version). Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance. https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12598 Packet checked 2026-10-05 at Abstract; comments identifying the 2021 workshop version. Evidence: Combines conditional and unconditional score estimates to trade sample quality against diversity without a separate classifier. Scope limit: A guidance method; stronger conditioning does not establish exact geometry or labels.

[S8] Stability AI (2022). Stable Diffusion Public Release. https://stability.ai/news-updates/stable-diffusion-public-release Packet checked 2026-10-05 at 22 August release announcement; links to weights, code, public demo, and DreamStudio. Evidence: The public release connected downloadable weights and code with a public demo and DreamStudio access. Scope limit: A first-party release record supporting availability in 2022, not independent evidence of adoption, market share, or current capability.
